text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate and p95 tail on inference gRPC endpoints from az1a. 502/504 spikes + TCP resets observed. Trigger: p95>1200ms and grpc_stream_errors > 3x baseline.
oncall-maria: I'm on it. pulling logs now.
alex-eng: seeing connection reset spikes from instances in az1a: kernel rx drop + grpc backpressure in front of model pools.
jordan-se: customer impact: a handful of SLO customers in EU routed to az1a are seeing 5-20% error rates on generation calls. Noticable increase in latency for chat sessions.
oncall-maria: quick mitigation plan: 1) start draining new requests from az1a to eu-west-2b/eu-west-1, 2) scale up proxy pool in eu-west-2b, 3) enable model-fallback to smaller instance families where needed. doing step 1 now.
platform-bot: runbook step executed: set traffic_split for route /v1/generate -> {eu-west-2b: 0.6, eu-west-1: 0.4}. Command: `redwood traffic adjust --route generate --split eu-west-2b=0.6,eu-west-1=0.4`
oncall-maria: traffic shift executed, verifying health. p50 down, p95 still elevated for existing connections. New sessions showing improvement.
alex-eng: digging into instance metrics: affected workers show large `grpc_send_queue` backlog and repeated `ENETUNREACH`/`ECONNRESET`. KVCaches for models are being evicted frequently due to OOMs during coldstarts of quantized variants.
sre-lead-ben: hitting cloud provider ticket now. Notifying AWS: suspected single-AZ network plane intermittency + noisy host causing host-level NIC queue saturation. Ticket: 1234567890 opened.
jordan-se: raising customer comms: flagged top 10 accounts on EU routes, engineering note ready. Recommend telling them we routed traffic to other AZs and are monitoring.
oncall-maria: mitigation step 2: we are cordoning 3 suspect hosts and triggering graceful drain: `kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Starting now.
alex-eng: while draining, observed coldstart spike in model loads on target AZs. I'm toggling model-loading-rate-limit to 10/s to prevent kvcache thrash. `POST /internal/limits {"model_load_rate":10}`
platform-bot: config applied: model_load_rate=10 for region eu-west-2b.
next-oncall-lee: I'll take next 30m of oncall. any remaining customer impact?
jordan-se: errors dropped to ~1-2% for impacted routes post-traffic-shift. Some long-lived sessions may still see resets until they reconnect.
oncall-maria: AWS responded: confirmed host-level packet drops and NIC transmit queue pressure, they recommend instance replacement. Coordinating live replacement; ETA for rolling replacements is ~18 mins for current batch.
sre-lead-ben: plan: continue traffic shift to keep steady-state <1% errors, finish draining suspect hosts, replace hosts with vendor, then gradually move traffic back if stable.
alex-eng: watchpoints for post-recovery: warm kvcache sizes, p95 token throughput, and grpc_stream_retries. I'll set alert: if p95>600ms for 10m -> page.
platform-bot: alert rule created: inference.p95 > 600ms for 600s -> page oncall.
next-oncall-lee: acknowledged handoff. leaving coordinated channel, will monitor and escalate to infradev if needed.
oncall-maria: moving to postmortem capture: saving logs `s3://redwood-incidents/4999123456/logs.tar.gz` and capturing customer impact table.
jordan-se: customer comms sent to affected accounts: short note + mitigation steps + ETA for postmortem.
sre-lead-ben: nice work. we should run a follow-up: 1) run canary with small % back to az1a after host replacement, 2) review autoscaler behaviour during node replacements, 3) investigate kvcache eviction patterns during coldstart. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
oncall-maria: handing off full incident ownership to ben for postmortem. I'm available for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (errors back to baseline, traffic shifted). Paging closed.
summary: Live coordination of an az1a single-AZ network/instance degradation affecting inference gRPC endpoints. Actions: traffic shift, node drain/replacement, model load rate limiting, customer comms, AWS ticket.
